question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

She talked enormous/ of what she wanted / from her education.
solution:
The correct answer is: **She talked enormous**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is in the first part of the sentence, where "**enormous**" is used incorrectly as an adverb instead of an adjective.
 
• An adverb is a word that modifies or describes a verb, adjective, adverb, or even a whole sentence.
 
• **Adverbs **provide additional information about how, when, where, why, or to what degree something is happening.
 
• In this context, the correct word should be "**enormously**," which is an adverb and modifies the verb "**talked**."
 
• Here, "**enormously**" describes how she talked about what she wanted from her education, indicating a high degree or intensity of discussion.

**The corrected sentence would be**: "*She talked enormously of what she wanted from her education.*"

Hence, **option 1** is the correct answer.
